28: NIKÍTA. Eh! There he goes rambling! Come to the table.
26: AKÍM. I can't, I mean can't what d'ye call it, can't drink tea. Because of your filth, I mean; I feel what d'ye call it, I feel sick, very sick! I can't what d'ye call it, I can't drink tea with you.
25: NIKÍTA. Sit down and drink your tea, and have done with it!
24: AKÍM [ excited ] Past! No, lad, it's not past. Sin, I mean, fastens on to sin—drags sin after it, and you've stuck fast, Nikíta, fast in sin! Stuck fast in sin! I see you're fast in sin. Stuck fast, sunk in sin, I mean!
23: AKÍM. I told you, what d'ye call it, I told you about the orphan lass. That you had wronged an orphan—Marína, I mean, wronged her! NIKÍTA. Eh! he's at it again. Let bygones be bygones … All that's past!
22: AKÍM. Ruin, ruin; you're in the midst of it! What did I tell you that time? NIKÍTA. You said all sorts of things!
21: NIKÍTA. What ruin? Just prove it!
19: AKÍM. Nothing what d'ye call it, nothing has offended me, nothing at all! I mean only, I see, what d'you call it, I mean, I see my son, to ruin I mean, to ruin, I mean my son's on the road to ruin, I mean.
18: NIKÍTA. Eh now! Have done talking! Sit down and drink your tea! ANÍSYA. Why, father, you'll shame us before the neighbours. What has offended you?
16: AKÍM [ fastens his belt ] Going, because, I mean, it's not right in your house, I mean, what d'you call it, not right, Nikíta, in the house, what d'ye call it, not right! I mean, you are living a bad life, Nikíta, bad,—I'll go.
15: NIKÍTA. But are you going without having any tea?
14: AKÍM. I can't, I mean what d'ye call 'em, in your house, what d'ye call 'em, can't stay I mean, stay, can't stay, forgive me.
13: NIKÍTA. My gracious! Where are you going to at this time of night?
12: NIKÍTA [ does not see the money ] Why have you put on your things? AKÍM. I'm going, going I mean; forgive me for the Lord's sake. [ Takes up his cap and belt ].
10: AKÍM [ gets down and puts on his sheepskin, then comes up to the table and puts down the money ] Here, take your money back! Put it away.
8: NIKÍTA. Here on the table. Well! have you been to the Elder? Ah, that's it! Have your say and then eat your words. Now then, that's enough. Don't be cross, sit down and drink this. [ Fills a wine-glass for her ] And here's your present. [ Gives her the parcel he had been sitting on. Anísya takes it silently and shakes her head ].
7: Silence. Akím sits on the oven and winds the bands round his legs. Enter Anísya with samovár. ANÍSYA. Where shall I put it?
6: AKOULÍNA. The tea things? All right. [ Brings the things ].
5: NIKÍTA. Oh, that's it! Call her, and tell her to bring the samovár. And you, Akoulína, get the tea things.
4: NAN. She's standing and crying out there in the passage.
0: NAN [ to Akoulína ] Sister, the samovár is just boiling over.
